title: Hearth of Stone
shortDescription: Granite takes the weight and does not complain.
longDescription:
The Hearth of Stone is a vaulted room that feels older than the hall that leads to it. Granite blocks fit as if they had chosen one another. Dust hangs in cool light. A carved keystone watches the door. The air smells of wet rock after rain and the faint chalk of a mason's mark.
Mentor Quern stands like another block that learned to speak.

fixtures.name: Mentor Quern
fixtures.lookDescription: A massive grey badger with granite-dusted paws and a mason's belt. Try talk quern.
fixtures.examineDescription: Quern's stripe is pale with stone-dust. The belt is heavy. He does not hurry a sentence, and he does not drop one.
fixtures.dialogue: "Stone holds. Look this hearth — the keystone, the blocks that chose one another. Find Flint in the South Orchard. Come back when you have stood somewhere that did not shift."

welcome.text: "I am Quern. Set your paws. The floor will wait. Stone teaches you to hold — not to boast, not to hurry a wall that is already doing its work. Look this hearth. See how the keystone carries the weight without a speech. Then walk to the South Orchard, where the grass is springy and Flint keeps a dummy that has taken more honest blows than most first-years. Attack it once. Return and talk to me. I will be here. Stone does not wander."

craft.text: "A wall that boasts is already failing. First you look at what is already holding. Then you strike a thing that is meant to be struck — Flint's dummy, under the apple boughs, not a classmate who did not agree. Then you come back, and we will see whether your feet remembered the floor."

go.text: "Look the keystone. Carry the weight you named. Then find the orchard south of Lantern Court. I will be here."

lessons-done.text: "You have looked. You have stood in the orchard. Stone has your name, and your kit is open. Alder waits in the High Study with a question about the bell below — an old note the beams still carry, like a cart over wet cobbles. Go up when you are ready. Do not rush his oak. It has held longer than you have."

fixtures.name: Carved Keystone
fixtures.examineDescription: The keystone is plain except for a shallow mark like a held breath. The blocks around it have not shifted. A slate says: 'Carry the weight you named.'
